questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) A technician wants to set up a local area network (LAN).

(i) Name four basic networking equipment that can be used and the principal function of each of them. (8 marks)

(ii) The technician decides to set up a client-server network. Give two advantages of the technician's choice. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Four networking devices and their functions (8 marks, 2 marks each: 1 for the name, 1 for the function)**

| Equipment | Principal function |
|---|---|
| Network interface card (NIC) | Fitted in each computer; it connects the computer to the network cable or to the wireless signal and converts the computer's data into signals that can travel on the network. |
| Switch | Central connection point of a LAN; it receives data from one computer and forwards it only to the computer it is addressed to (it uses the MAC address). |
| Hub | Simple connection point that joins several computers together; it copies the data it receives to all the other connected computers. |
| Router | Connects the LAN to another network, such as the Internet, and chooses the path along which data packets are sent. |
| Network cable (twisted pair / UTP) | Transmission medium that carries the signals between the devices and the switch or hub. |

(Any four are accepted. A wireless access point, which lets wireless devices join the LAN, and a modem, which links the network to an Internet service provider, are also accepted.)

**(ii) Two advantages of a client-server network (2 marks, 1 mark each)**

- Security and user accounts are managed centrally on the server (one place to set passwords and access rights).
- Files and data are stored on the server, so they are shared easily and backed up from one place.
- Resources such as printers and software are shared and controlled centrally, and a powerful dedicated server serves many clients faster and more reliably.

(Any two.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Briefly explain the following computing terms and state an example of each.

(i) Integrated Development Environment (2 marks)

(ii) Compiled language (2 marks)

(iii) Interpreted language (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Integrated Development Environment (IDE) (2 marks).** A software application that brings together, in one window, the tools a programmer needs to build a program: a source-code editor, a compiler or interpreter, a debugger and tools to run the program. *Examples:* Code::Blocks, Dev-C++, Free Pascal Lazarus, Visual Studio, Eclipse.

**(ii) Compiled language (2 marks).** A programming language whose source program is translated all at once by a compiler into machine code (an executable file) before the program is run; the executable then runs without the compiler. *Examples:* C, C++, Pascal.

**(iii) Interpreted language (2 marks).** A programming language whose source program is translated and executed one statement at a time by an interpreter each time it is run; no separate executable file is produced. *Examples:* Python, BASIC, JavaScript.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) In the email address admin-cgceboard@gmail.com

(i) Identify the username and the domain name. (2 marks)

(ii) What is the difference between the Internet and the WWW? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Username and domain name (2 marks).** An email address has the form *username@domain name*. The part before the @ sign is the **username**: `admin-cgceboard`. The part after the @ sign is the **domain name**: `gmail.com`.

**(ii) Internet and WWW (2 marks).** The **Internet** is the worldwide network of interconnected computer networks (the cables, routers, servers and the TCP/IP rules that link them). It carries many services such as email, file transfer and the web. The **World Wide Web (WWW)** is only one of these services: a collection of linked web pages and other documents, stored on web servers, that we reach with a web browser using URLs and the HTTP protocol. In short, the Internet is the infrastructure and the WWW is a service that runs on it.
